name: Ada Lovelace
facts: Ada Lovelace was born in 1815 and studied advanced mathematics.
She documented Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine and published extensive notes about it in 1843.
Her notes included a table describing how the Analytical Engine could calculate Bernoulli numbers, often described as an early computer program.

name: Alan Turing
facts: Alan Turing completed the draft of his paper On Computable Numbers in 1936, work foundational to computer science.
During the Second World War he worked at Bletchley Park as part of the effort to decipher Enigma communications.
His 1950 paper Computing Machinery and Intelligence examined artificial intelligence and introduced what became known as the Turing test.

name: Grace Hopper
facts: Grace Hopper programmed the Harvard Mark I during the Second World War.
She published an early paper on compilers and advocated programming languages based on English words.
She was instrumental in the development of COBOL and retired from the United States Navy with the rank of rear admiral.

name: Margaret Hamilton
facts: Margaret Hamilton led the Software Engineering Division of the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory.
Her division developed onboard flight software for NASA's Apollo program.
Hamilton has been credited with helping popularize the term software engineering.

name: Barbara Liskov
facts: Barbara Liskov led the design of the CLU programming language, which advanced data abstraction.
She and Jeannette Wing formulated the Liskov substitution principle for reasoning about subtype behavior.
Liskov received the 2008 ACM A.M. Turing Award for contributions to programming language and system design.

name: Donald Knuth
facts: Donald Knuth is the author of the multi-volume series The Art of Computer Programming.
He made major contributions to the analysis of algorithms and the design of programming languages.
Knuth created the TeX typesetting system and received the 1974 ACM A.M. Turing Award.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
facts: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN in 1989.
He wrote the first web client and web server in 1990 and developed early specifications for URIs, HTTP, and HTML.
He founded the World Wide Web Consortium in 1994 to develop interoperable web standards.

name: Radia Perlman
facts: Radia Perlman designed the spanning tree algorithm that enabled Ethernet networks to scale.
She designed IS-IS, a link-state routing protocol that continues to be used for routing IP.
She later designed TRILL to improve bandwidth use in Ethernet networks.

name: Geoffrey Hinton
facts: Geoffrey Hinton made foundational contributions to machine learning with artificial neural networks.
His work included the Boltzmann machine, which learns characteristic elements from data.
He shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for foundational discoveries and inventions enabling machine learning with artificial neural networks.

name: Fei-Fei Li
facts: Fei-Fei Li is a professor in Stanford University's Computer Science Department and a founding co-director of Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute.
She directed the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory from 2013 to 2018.
She created ImageNet and the ImageNet Challenge, a large-scale dataset and benchmark important to modern computer vision.
